name: vault-rohit-local-ai-without-the-cloud
title: Rohit - Local AI Without the Cloud
speaker: Rohit - Local AI Without the Cloud

chapters.title: Opening Remarks
chapters.caption: The presenter welcomes the audience and sets the stage for the talk, emphasizing the importance of local AI and data sovereignty.

chapters.title: WebAI Introduction
chapters.caption: Rohit introduces WebAI, highlighting its focus on local AI models and real-world applications like airport bag tracking.

chapters.title: Local AI Benefits
chapters.caption: The speaker explains how local AI enables data control, privacy, and cost efficiency through on-premises deployment.

chapters.title: Developer Perspective
chapters.caption: Rohit shares his developer viewpoint, emphasizing open-source tools and leveraging existing hardware for AI tasks.

chapters.title: Agent Cost Issues
chapters.caption: The talk highlights how AI agents can multiply costs through hidden calls and redundant reasoning steps.

chapters.title: Cloud vs Local
chapters.caption: A comparison is made between cloud-based and local AI, stressing data privacy, predictable costs, and offline functionality.

chapters.title: Model Selection
chapters.caption: Guidance is provided on choosing the right inference engine based on hardware, such as MLX for MacBooks or VLLM for GPUs.

chapters.title: Seamless Integration
chapters.caption: The speaker demonstrates how existing cloud workflows can be switched to local models with minimal changes via OpenAI-compatible endpoints.

chapters.title: Efficiency Evidence
chapters.caption: Data from prior presentations supports the claim that most tasks can be handled efficiently by smaller, local models.

chapters.title: Page Retention Basics
chapters.caption: Introduces page retention as a core memory organization concept, comparing it to OS paging and highlighting Mac's advantages in managing multiple Chrome tabs.

chapters.title: Radix Attention & Caching
chapters.caption: Explains Radix attention's use of tree-structured cache for token reuse, reducing recomputation and boosting speed in agentic and RAG workflows.

chapters.title: Continuous Batching & Memory
chapters.caption: Describes continuous batching and efficient memory management through OS-like paging, minimizing compute waste and enabling high GPU utilization.

chapters.title: Model Size & Quantization
chapters.caption: Discusses model size reduction via 4-bit quantization and the benefits of Mixture of Experts (MoE) models for faster inference with fewer active parameters.

chapters.title: Performance & Real-World Use
chapters.caption: Compares token-per-second speeds across models, emphasizing that local AI is fast enough for daily tasks like reading and email, even with smaller models.

chapters.title: Local AI & Hardware
chapters.caption: Highlights the long-term value of local AI on MacBooks, leveraging unified memory and avoiding additional GPU costs for sustained performance.

chapters.title: Speech-to-Text & Open Source
chapters.caption: Shares a personal setup using a local, open-source speech-to-text app that runs without internet, with minimal RAM and fast load times.

chapters.title: Conclusion
chapters.caption: Wraps up the talk by affirming the practicality and efficiency of local AI, with open-source tools and optimized models enabling powerful, private, and fast workflows.
